findings.title: `prisma` is used but never imported in the Salesforce calendar service
findings.body: `getClient` now calls `prisma.credential.update(...)`, but the file's import list has no `prisma` import (only jsforce, rrule, zod, CalEventParser, constants, http-error, logger, types, getAppKeysFromSlug, parseRefreshTokenResponse). This is a ReferenceError at runtime and a type error at build time, so every Salesforce calendar operation fails.

findings.title: Salesforce now refreshes its token on every client construction, bypassing the sync endpoint
findings.body: `getClient` unconditionally POSTs to login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token and writes the result to the DB, for every user and every service instantiation. It does not go through `refreshOAuthTokens`, so self-hosters with `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` never get their sync endpoint used for Salesforce, and non-sync installs gain an extra network round trip and a DB write each time. Its `statusText !== "OK"` check is also brittle, since HTTP/2 responses may have an empty statusText.

findings.title: Minimum token schema uses a computed key from `z.string().toString()`, which is not a pattern
findings.body: `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` builds an object key from a schema's string representation (a fixed literal such as "[object Object]"), not a wildcard for 'any numeric property'. The resulting schema requires a property with that literal name, so real token responses fail `safeParse`. In sync mode every refresh then throws 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned'. The same applies to the `[z.string().optional().toString()]` entry on line 10.

findings.title: Real refresh token is overwritten with the placeholder string "refresh_token"
findings.body: When the parsed response lacks `refresh_token` (the minimum schema strips it, and it is absent from many refresh responses), this code sets it to the literal "refresh_token". The caller then persists that value to the credential, destroying the working refresh token. The sync-mode check here also uses only the global env flag, while `refreshOAuthTokens` additionally requires a userId, so for team-owned credentials (userId null) the real refresh path runs but the minimum schema still strips fields and the placeholder still gets written.

findings.title: Sync branch returns a raw fetch Response while the other branch returns the provider's token shape
findings.body: The sync path returns the `fetch` Response, but the non-sync path returns the value of `refreshFunction()`, which callers expect in provider-specific shapes (e.g. Google reads `res.data`, Zoho reads `tokenInfo.data.error`, HubSpot reads `expiresIn`). With sync enabled, Google's `res?.data` is undefined, so `token.access_token` throws. That error is swallowed by the catch, and the stale token is returned silently. Zoho Bigin's `tokenInfo.data.error` throws an uncaught TypeError in `refreshAccessToken`, breaking event creation. The sync response is also never checked for `response.ok`, so an error from the sync endpoint is handled as if it were a successful token refresh.

findings.title: Expiry computed from `expires_in` becomes NaN when sync mode omits that field
findings.body: After switching to `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, in sync mode the parsed data may not contain `expires_in`. `Date.now() + newTokens.expires_in * 1000` is then NaN. The stored `expiry_date` becomes NaN, and `isTokenValid` (`(expires_in || expiry_date) < Date.now()`) evaluates false, so the adapter never refreshes the token again.

findings.title: Decrypted keys are unvalidated and JSON.parse can throw an unhandled error
findings.body: `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` is not wrapped in try/catch, so a wrong key or malformed payload produces an unstructured 500. The parsed value is then written directly to `credential.key` with no per-app schema check, so any JSON shape is stored and can break the app's CalendarService when it later parses the credential.

findings.title: Webhook secret compared with non-constant-time `!==`
findings.body: The shared secret from the request header is compared with `!==` against the env value. This is a timing-sensitive comparison for an authentication secret; `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers should be used. The header lookup also depends on the configured header name being lowercase, which Node enforces for incoming headers.

findings.title: New webhook endpoint and token-refresh changes have no tests
findings.body: The PR adds an authenticated endpoint that writes credentials, plus new refresh logic in parseRefreshTokenResponse and refreshOAuthTokens that branches on env vars and userId. The checklist confirms no tests were added. The bugs above (placeholder refresh token, NaN expiry, the broken schema) would be caught by unit tests on these helpers.

findings.title: Moved OAuth utilities may leave other importers of the old paths broken
findings.body: encodeOAuthState, decodeOAuthState and createOAuthAppCredential were moved to `_utils/oauth/`. Only the listed app files were updated. If other apps or shared code still import `_utils/encodeOAuthState`, `_utils/decodeOAuthState` or `_utils/createOAuthAppCredential`, they will fail at build time. The diff does not show a full repository search.
